ANTLRWorks (2008) demonstrates visual grammar debugging to help developers inspect parser behavior [1]. Compiler Explorer provides browser-based compilation with visible compiler output [2]. Flex and Bison supply the scanner and parser generation used in traditional Lex/Yacc workflows [3, 4]. Together, these references motivate Lexora's focus on a dedicated teaching workspace that combines native specification execution with a separate analyzer for program structure and intermediate code.
Related work: ANTLRWorks [1], Compiler Explorer [2], Flex and Bison [3, 4].

[1] Bovet, J. and Parr, T. (2008). ANTLRWorks: an ANTLR grammar development environment. Software: Practice and Experience, 38(12), 1305-1332. https://doi.org/10.1002/spe.872
[2] Compiler Explorer, official project documentation. https://github.com/compiler-explorer/compiler-explorer/blob/main/docs/WhatIsCompilerExplorer.md
[3] Flex manual. https://westes.github.io/flex/manual/Introduction.html
[4] GNU Bison manual. https://www.gnu.org/s/bison/manual/bison.html
The final sentence is a design synthesis from the reviewed approaches, rather than a claim that no comparable website exists. Lexora native execution and its educational analyzer remain separate.

The screenshot is the actual AST view for calculator stdin 3 + 5 * 2 followed by newline. The AST comes from Lexora’s own parser. It does not trace the uploaded grammar.
The analyzer visits the syntax tree. Declarations create entries, and references mark names as used.
Nested scopes control name lookup. Undeclared names and duplicate declarations produce errors.
The table records declarations and usage, rather than live runtime values.

Project evidence: backend/services/semanticAnalyzer.js and backend/services/inputAnalysis.js. Observed input: int x = 2 + 3 * 4; int y = x + 1;. Both global variables are declared. x is read and y is not read. The AST traversal creates records and marks references. Scope lookup uses a stack of Maps. A separate observation of int x = missing + 1; reports missing as used before declaration / assignment. This is educational analysis, independent of the submitted grammar.

name: Rectangle 7
text: Use isolated execution workers with restricted file and network access before public deployment.

Current evidence: backend/services/wslRunner.js uses wsl.exe -d Ubuntu -- bash on Windows and a native Bash process on Linux. timeout limits child command execution. backend/services/tempDir.js creates separate temporary job folders. These controls do not constitute a dedicated security sandbox. The analyzer covers a supported C subset, independently from the submitted .l/.y grammar. Expanded syntax, grammar-linked visualization, and isolated public execution workers are future work.
